newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan carrier says asylum flight chartered.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan carrier says asylum flight chartered.

text.p: A Turkmenistan Airlines plane carrying 173 Sri Lankan Tamils which made an unauthorised flight to the Netherlands had been chartered in Dubai, an airline official said opn Tuesday.

The plane was allowed to land at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport on Sunday after the pilot signalled he was running out of fuel. The 173 Sri Lankan Tamils on board subsequently applied for political asylum.
The Dutch government said it had grounded the plane until the Turkmen aviation authorities explained why it had been allowed to make an unauthorised flight to the Netherlands.

"Yes, we know the dispute will be over once the Turkmen side has paid penalties," the official told Reuters. "But Turkmenistan Airlines has simply been let down by a customer in Dubai who chartered this Dubai-Ashgabat-Amsterdam flight."
The official added: "We had permission from the airport in Amsterdam, although it was not coordinated with its director. Usually no problems arise in similar cases."
The passengers are to be allowed to stay in reception centres in the Netherlands while their requests for politcal asylum are processed.
The Dutch courts have stipulated that anyone from Sri Lanka who applies for asylum is entitled to a full hearing process, which can take years to complete.
The Sri Lankan government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in a 14-year war for independence by minority Tamils in the north of the island. Tamil groups say the toll is much higher.
